findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: The ice machine is observed with mold/build-up present on the ice machine baffle on the lower lip and on the top sealed portion inside the machine. Ensure these areas are cleaned and sanitized to remove the current build-up of debris and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. For the top portion of the ice machine, the existing caulking will need to be scrapped, the area cleaned and sanitized, and then a new seal placed. This was observed on the 4/25/2024 inspection report and an additional follow-up-sup is being scheduled for 5/16/2024. 
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
A large number of German roaches are observed in all life stages throughout the facility again this morning, especially in the "hot spots" identified yesterday near the door from the dining are to the kitchen, near the ice machine at the drive thru area, around the sandwich prep area and on the food contact surfaces of the sandwich prep area, around floor drains, along floor/wall junctions throughout the kitchen and on walls and shelves. Terminix has sprayed and baited the kitchen areas, and more it is evident that some of the roaches are in the dying process; however, there are still too numerous of live juveniles throughout the kitchen. Facility will voluntarily remain closed until live roaches are no longer observed in the food prep and food storage areas. Once live roaches are no longer observed in food prep areas, facility will call SCDPH to schedule the next follow-up before re-opening.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

Multiple juveniles were observed throughout the facility. Multiple glue traps throughout the facility with many dead and alive roaches in all life stages.  Facility voluntarily closed at 11:15 am. Contact pest control operator as soon as possible. Last visit from Terminex was 9/25/14 and were scheduled to return 10/9/14.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Baked potatoes in bottom holding drawer had internal temperatures of 115F and surface temperatures of 117F. Baked potatoes were just made today, and all potatoes in warmer were at +150F. Store manager noticed the temperature on the bottom drawer was only at 120F. Temperature of the drawer was turned up, and potatoes were discarded in the trash. Employee was advised on maintaining hot foods at 135F/above after reaching proper heating temperatures. The temperature inside the drawer went up above 140F after setting was adjusted, so hot holding drawer is functioning properly. Potentially hazardous foods (PHF) held hot shall be maintained at 135F/above. Maintain hot PHF at proper temperature at all times.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text: 750.210 - Portioned BBQ in bottom hot holding drawer had internal temperatures of 78F-88F and surface temperatures of 90F-95F. Employee stated products were placed in bottom holding drawer directly from walkin cooler. BBQ was discarded. Proper reheating was discussed with the employee and management. Employee stated the BBQ is heated in the microwave prior to serving and would just be held cold until orders are needed rather than heating in advance. PHF shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout using equipment intended for reheating (i.e. oven, microwave, etc.). Warmers and hot holding drawers are intended for holding foods at 135F/above once they have already been heated using proper equipment to rapidly get products to 165F/above. Properly reheat foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

C) drive thru - 1) soda machine below ice bin (lids, roach egg cases, dead roaches, & debris); 2) syrup storage cabinet (syrup splash, dead roaches, & debris); & 3) cabinet below cash register (roaches, feces, debris); D) metal storage bin at side of front counter holding fry cups, bags, & ZAPtimer; E) white fan on make line (dust); F) inside storage drawer at back prep table; & G) motor storage cabinets at lobby drink counter. Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained

It appeared to be coming off of a line connected to the motor. Water was accumulating on the floor in front of the soda machine. Make all necessary repairs to the drive thru soda machine (i.e. repair motor, make sure ice bin has proper seals so water is not dripping, etc.). All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Live roaches were observed in the drive thru area - adult walking across the floor and juveniles around electrical cords in cabinet below cash machine. Adult was caught by inspector with napkin and crushed/discarded in trash after showing store manager. Shift manager on duty stated he saw a couple roaches in the drive thru over the weekend. Hatched egg cases were observed in the lower compartment below the ice bin at the soda machine. Feces (looked like grains of pepper) were observed where juveniles were present. Thoroughly clean all areas where roaches were observed as well as the floor and floor drain in the drive thru (see #23 & #36 for details). Contact Terminix for additional treatment as well (see general comments)

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

Go through the entire facility, starting with the drive thru, and properly seal all holes to eliminate potential hiding places for pests.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 7501350, 1390, & 1160 - A) Conditions in the lower compartment of the drive thru soda machine have allowed for the proliferation of roaches in the area. Thoroughly clean and make necessary repairs to eliminate presence of roaches (see #23, 36, & 35a). B) Old cutting board was observed on the floor below dry storage shelves. A manager stated at previous inspections the cutting board was to be discarded. Get rid of the cutting board. Only article necessary for the operation/maintenance of the facility should be stored on-site. Remove all unnecessary items. C) Wet mop was observed with head down inside the mop sink. Store wet mops hanging or inverted between uses to allow for proper drying. Wet mop heads can serve as a food/water source for pests.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text: 750.290 - Blue ice scoop holder on top of ice machine had standing water in it (~1inch) and small pieces of floating debris. Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. Maintain the ice scoop holder clean. **Manager cleaned/sanitized the ice scoop holder during the inspection.**

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750.820c - (R) Underside of chicken racks observed inside hot holding drawers on prep line had buildup on it. All utensils and equipment shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil. Properly pre-soak & pre-scrape equipment before ware washing process. If soil remains repeat the process until the equipment in question has been properly cleaned/sanitized and all gross soil has been removed. If equipment can not be maintained in a sanitary condition then replace it with equipment that is easier to maintain.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Soda nozzles/diffusers observed soaking at the lobby soda counter were soiled. Some of the nozzles/diffusers had chunky mold buildup. Foods shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times. Nozzles/diffusers were properly cleaned/sanitized during the inspection. **Just soaking soda nozzles/diffusers will not prevent buildup of mold. They must be properly washed, rinse, and sanitized like all other food contact surfaces. Pop the inner diffusers out of nozzles and use a small scrub brush that is adequate to clean inside small holes/crevices. Make these part of the routine cleaning schedule**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750.650a - Plastic ice scoop at drive thru and large metal scoop at back ice machine were both damaged. Both scoops had cracks in them. The large scoop was also worn/jagged on the food contact surface end that comes in contact with the ice as it is being scooped. Replace the ice scoops. findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750.820c - Underside of chicken rack observed inside hot holding drawers on prep line had buildup on it. If soil remains repeat the process until the equipment in question has been properly cleaned/sanitized and all gross soil has been removed. If equipment can not be maintained in a sanitary condition then replace it with equipment that is easier to maintain.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750.830: Upon arrival at inspection, the sanitizer concentration in the 3rd sink and in a bucket, was 0 ppm Quat.  A new sanitizer is being used by the establishment since last inspection.  The sink and bucket were emptied and sanitizer placed in the sink again and re-filled.  The concentration was extremely too high, over 400 ppm (bottle suggests 150 ppm), so water was removed and we started over again with just water.  Cap full, by cap full the sanitizer was added and I determined by the facility's test strips and by mine, that no more than 2-3 cap fulls of sanitizer be added to the sink that when filled is approx. 20-25 gallons.  The bottle of sanitizer "Ster-O-Kem #15 with organic soil tolerance" produced by Damon Industries from Alliance, OH 1-800-362-9850 suggests 3/4 oz. per 1 gallon of water.  If this were to be followed, it would cause the concentration to be toxic when used in this manner (3 part sink).  Concentration was corrected during inspection.  *Violation Corrected*
